quotes.speaker: Kon Knueppel
quotes.summary_phrase: Kon Knueppel on his transition to the NBA and preseason challenges
quotes.excerpt: I got no chance. The footwork is, the footwork is, I don't know, it was a preseason game.
quotes.quote: I'd say that all of a sudden I was guarding SGA in transition. I was just like, man, I got no chance. The footwork is, the footwork is, I don't know, it was a preseason game and I was just like, oh my goodness. I picked this guy up. quotes.speaker: Kon Knueppel
quotes.summary_phrase: Kon Knueppel on being a Milwaukee Brewers fan during the World Series
quotes.excerpt: This is the best place I've ever been for baseball, being a Brewers fan.
quotes.quote: This is the best place I've ever been for baseball, being a Brewers fan. Being in the World Series is where you want to be. The Rays just got it done last night, so now I'm officially nervous. I was feeling good there for about a week when we were already in and we didn't know who we were going to play. Now I'm officially nervous. Rays are really good. Two best teams, but it should be a great series.

quotes.speaker: Kon Knueppel
quotes.summary_phrase: Kon Knueppel on the Cleveland Guardians' playoff run and the team's approach
quotes.excerpt: If you're trying out Scoubel, Yamamoto, Snell, and Glassnow in four straight games, you should not be getting swept.
quotes.quote: I think Cleveland obviously had a good run, but super excited for the crew. Probably my favorite team I'm rooting for ever. If you're trying out Scoubel, Yamamoto, Snell, and Glassnow in four straight games, you should not be getting swept. And so, how do you get swept? All credit to Murphy and the guys being ready to play, and their approach, like Bauer's played approach. The pitchers, the bullpen, how they approach, I'm going to win this pitch, or just take it pitch by pitch, and then getting to those 3-2 counts and winning those 3-2 counts. I just think that mental approach of being very present, staying in what you can control at this moment, which is each pitch. I just see that, you know, last year when they got to the NLCS and got swept by the Dodgers, you're out there forcing, you're trying to make plays, where today they're just like, take your walks, get on base, look at every pitch. I think it was just really fun as a fan to watch that way, because they want that free base. They want to force those counts, and I mean, for me, that's fun to watch as a fan. Maybe not everybody's cup of tea, but for me, that's what I enjoy.

quotes.speaker: Tommy Alter
quotes.summary_phrase: Tommy Alter on the Dodgers' dominance and the team's sustained intensity
quotes.excerpt: It's one thing to win 103 games, but it's another thing with this level to keep this level up.
quotes.quote: It's one thing to win 103 games, but it's another thing with this level to keep this level up, because I feel like objectively, normally when you guys get to this place in October, it feels like the gas starts to empty a little bit. And this year so far, it's felt like the opposite has happened, the throttle has sort of continued.

quotes.speaker: Kon Knueppel
quotes.summary_phrase: Kon Knueppel on watching the Padres' walk-off win with teammates
quotes.excerpt: I was at my house with Pat Connaughton and Grayson Allen, we were watching Red Zone.
quotes.quote: I was at my house with Pat Connaughton and Grayson Allen, we were watching Red Zone and I had the Brewers game on, too. We stood up and Pat Connaughton cares a little bit about the Brewers, you know, being in Milwaukee for a long time. Grayson Allen didn't really care as much, until that last inning when we were watching.

quotes.speaker: Tommy Alter
quotes.summary_phrase: Tommy Alter on the intensity of playoff baseball and the 'Moneyball' memes
quotes.excerpt: That was what makes playoff baseball great in a nutshell. That whole at-bat.
quotes.quote: That was what makes playoff baseball great in a nutshell. That whole at-bat. The level of intensity, 10 pitches, 11 pitches, and him staying alive in that was such a microcosm for what makes the whole experience so just great for the fan. Did you see all the Moneyball memes with the music from Moneyball? I don't know who started doing that, but it makes it so much better. They were doing it with you guys and they were doing it with when Jose Ramirez had that. That's what's cool about this playoffs. I have a bunch of friends who are Guardians fans, I'm bummed for them, they couldn't get to the series, but just like, it's cool all the new heroes in this run. Even the White Sox, even the White Sox doing what they did, like we don't need the Dodgers anymore. It was great with Toronto last year, but just having these new faces, having, having these guys who are like, I'm not sure how many casual fans, I think they probably knew what was doing, just because of the level that he was doing it at, but I'm not sure how many games they were watching this year. And so this getting that exposure to these sort of like new faces, outside of the history of the franchise and what it means to the franchise, I think is just a cool thing for the sport.

quotes.speaker: Kon Knueppel
quotes.summary_phrase: Kon Knueppel on Jake Bauers' journey and impact on the Brewers
quotes.excerpt: Jake Bauers was like a journeyman, he almost retired, and all of a sudden he's NLCS MVP.
quotes.quote: Jake Bauers was like a journeyman, he almost retired, and all of a sudden he's NLCS MVP with two of the best at-bats I've ever seen. Like that sort of stuff is awesome to me about baseball. It's cool, especially when you see like rookies like Prad and Lara like really take, you know, like take it so seriously coming in as rookies and like really, really feeling that for Milwaukee already, that love.

quotes.speaker: Tommy Alter
quotes.summary_phrase: Tommy Alter on the challenges of the salary cap in professional sports
quotes.excerpt: It's hard, it's hard obviously, I mean this is going to be a big topic in the offseason.
quotes.quote: It's hard, it's hard obviously, I mean this is going to be a big topic in the offseason about the, you know, the, the salary cap or lack thereof, but there is also just a weird thing and I'm curious now, we talked about this a little bit with Yelich about their culture. I'm curious now, I think the thing that makes it trick, what's tricky with the Dodgers was like they, I mean they've done this last two years and it's worked out for them. So it's hard to say that they're, they're not doing something right, but they also, they kind of like mess around the whole year. It's like they have these guys who are on IL, I mean Otani's been slumping, which is a different thing, but they, it doesn't feel like they, you have any sense of the identity of their team until it gets to the playoffs and you're like, oh shit, now it's the Monstars again.

quotes.speaker: Kon Knueppel
quotes.summary_phrase: Kon Knueppel on the Packers' season and the loss to the Falcons
quotes.excerpt: It's been an interesting season so far. I mean like two different very prime time performances.
quotes.quote: It's been an interesting season so far. I mean like two different very prime time performances. Thursday night getting smacked around by the Falcons and then that was dark. That was dark. That was like, I think you might have a new coach. That was maybe the lowest I've been as a Packers fan. Like, man, I don't think we're very good. This might be the worst Packers team that I'll see. To in two weeks we're four and two and we have a like pretty much pretty dominating win against the Cowboys on Sunday night and we look good.

quotes.speaker: Tommy Alter
quotes.summary_phrase: Tommy Alter on the Bears' long-term struggles and the recent win
quotes.excerpt: That was a long time coming and I actually think with the Packers said after the game.
quotes.quote: That was a long time coming and I actually think with the Packers said after the game was not surprising. I think it was good for the Bears to go through that, Caleb or not. You know, I think we were getting beat either way. We were just talking, we were talking a lot and those games that we beat you guys in last year, both of the obviously both were like won by the skin of our teeth.

quotes.speaker: Kon Knueppel
quotes.summary_phrase: Kon Knueppel on the Packers-Bears rivalry and the playoff implications
quotes.excerpt: I mean, that's what you want. It's bragging rights. You won last year in the playoffs.
quotes.quote: I mean, that's what you want. It's bragging rights. You won last year in the playoffs. How often do the Packers and Bears meet in the playoffs? And we never win. We went on a long run. I mean, we won how many in a row? 10, 11 in a row.

quotes.speaker: Tommy Alter
quotes.summary_phrase: Tommy Alter on the intensity of the Packers-Bears rivalry
quotes.excerpt: I don't even remember the last, before last, that's what made last year so crazy.
quotes.quote: I don't even remember the last, before last, that's what made last year so crazy. It was like I don't even remember the last time we even beat you, period. Rodgers used to say that. I don't think we've ever beaten Rodgers. Like Rodgers was like maybe like 21 and four or something crazy.

quotes.speaker: Kon Knueppel
quotes.summary_phrase: Kon Knueppel on the Packers' recent performance and the team's outlook
quotes.excerpt: You beat us three times in the 2020s, and two times we had Malik Willis in for the majority.
quotes.quote: I mean, you beat us three times in the 2020s, and two times we had Malik Willis in for the majority of the game. And the third time was obviously a playoff collapse, which was thankfully I didn't get to see, because I was playing the Jazz. Yeah, we were playing the Jazz. But I ran out of halftime where we're up 21 to three and I was pumped and I ran out for the beginning of the game.

quotes.quote: Coby White's a great guy to be around. Just signed him to a big contract this off season. Brandon Miller just signed a big extension yesterday. So we're really pumped for him.

quotes.speaker: Kon Knueppel
quotes.summary_phrase: Kon Knueppel discusses leadership and team integration while injured
quotes.excerpt: I get assigned a guy each game right now to watch film with.
quotes.quote: We made some moves this off season. It's just a different group. We're trying to get everybody up to speed on the brand of basketball we want to play. It's been tough being injured and not being out there, but doing the best I can off of it, trying to be a leader, watch film with guys. That's been kind of a key. I get assigned a guy each game right now to watch film with.

quotes.speaker: Kon Knueppel
quotes.summary_phrase: Kon Knueppel praises Grayson Allen and Musa for offseason progress

quotes.quote: I really like the group we got. I think Grayson Allen's had a really good preseason. He'll be a big player for us. Musa's been an animal, put on a ton of muscle this off season.

quotes.speaker: Kon Knueppel
quotes.summary_phrase: Second year players developing into more comfortable NBA roles
quotes.excerpt: Year two is like, man, I feel I'm an established NBA player.
quotes.quote: Obviously Naz is around now, but like Seon and Liam and Colk, some of the guys that were rookies with me last year, just getting an off season under their belt, getting more comfortable as NBA players. I think that does a lot of good, just coming into year two. Year one you're just trying to figure stuff out, but year two is like, man, I feel I'm an established NBA player. I know what I can do.

quotes.quote: What was the, the guys he played with in high school? We did an app with him and we're talking about the Jelly Boy, the, the Jelly Fam from Jersey. Have you ever watched those old, have you ever watched those old clips? Yeah, I mean I used to when I was in like fifth grade.

quotes.speaker: Kon Knueppel
quotes.summary_phrase: Kon Knueppel on his rookie year experience and the learning curve
quotes.excerpt: I was telling Seely, our head coach, like last year I came into every day.
quotes.quote: I was telling Seely, our head coach, like last year I came into every day. We're at Queens College because we were getting our our practice facility/arena was getting done, redone. So, coming into Queens College and I was like, I was nervous. Every, every day. Like I I would kind of almost, not necessarily, dread but it would get to be like 9:00 p.m. the night before and I'm like, man, like I got to go, I got to make a good impression, like all this stuff. And I thoroughly enjoyed this summer because I came in like, I'm getting better at basketball today. This is fun. I love this. I think that's like the biggest adjustment, like if I could tell myself a year ago, just like, chill. Chill a little bit. Like it's going to be it's going to be all right. Like just just focus on what you can control, what you can work on, and less so about like, you know, what what are my teammates thinking of me? What are the coaches thinking of me? You know, like how am I am I going to carve out playing time? Am I playing well in our pickup games and stuff like that? Like, chill out a little bit and uh this is a time for you to get better and experiment and enjoy.
